How to read the scores

Scores run from 0 to 100, and higher is better. A category score is the weighted share of its checks that passed and of its measurements that scored well. The overall score is a weighted average of the categories that were measured.

  • 90 to 100 good
  • 50 to 89 needs improvement
  • 0 to 49 poor
Accessibility
Whether people who use a screen reader, keyboard, or other assistive technology can use the app. Measured by axe in this run.
Performance
How quickly the page loads and becomes usable. Measured by Lighthouse in this run.
Responsiveness
How smoothly frames render and how fast the app reacts to input. Measured by integration_test timeline in this run.
Memory
How much memory the app uses. Not measured in this run.
Best practices
General web practices such as HTTPS, console errors, and deprecated APIs. Not measured in this run.

Where the numbers come from:

  • Lighthouse 12.8.0: Google's page audit, run in Chrome, for load performance, best practices, and accessibility. Feeds Performance.
  • axe 4.10.3: accessibility rules checked in the browser on the rendered page. Feeds Accessibility.
  • integration_test timeline: frame build and raster times recorded by integration_test. Feeds Responsiveness.

Findings

Each finding names the rule that failed, the route it failed on, and the tool that reported it. A message that starts with "Needs review" is a check axe could not decide on its own, so a person has to look at it. Needs-review results are listed here but do not lower the score.
